Chili con Carne

A long-simmered chilli built on toasted whole spices and a hit of dark chocolate, with the beef cut into cubes rather than minced so it keeps its texture. Better on the second day, as all chillies are.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(2,911)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 2911 reviews 1 hr 50 min total Serves 6 servings Easy Mexican
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Toasting whole spices before grinding releases their volatile oils and creates new aromatic compounds through the Maillard reaction — a step that measurably deepens the finished chilli. Dark chocolate adds bitterness and body that balances the sweetness of the tomatoes without reading as chocolate.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Pat the beef dry and season. Brown it hard in the oil in a heavy pot, in three batches so the pan never crowds, about 5 minutes per batch. Set aside.

  2. Lower the heat and cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and peppers for 4 minutes more.

  3. Add all the ground spices and the oregano and cook, stirring, for 90 seconds until intensely fragrant.

  4. Stir in the tomato purée and chipotles and cook 2 minutes, then return the beef with any resting juices.

  5. Add the tomatoes, stock and salt. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook at 150°C / 300°F for 2 hours.

  6. Stir in the beans and cook uncovered for a further 30 minutes, until the sauce has reduced and the beef pulls apart.

  7. Off the heat, stir in the chocolate and vinegar. Taste and adjust the salt and acid.

  8. Rest for 20 minutes before serving — or better, cool and refrigerate overnight.

Chef’s Tips

  • Cubed chuck beats mince every time; you get texture instead of grit.
  • The vinegar at the end is what makes the flavours snap into focus. Do not skip it.
  • Serve the toppings separately: soured cream, grated cheese, spring onion, avocado, tortilla chips.

Pairing Suggestions

  • A dark Mexican beer or a Zinfandel
  • Serve with cornbread, rice or baked potatoes
  • Finish with lime sorbet

Storage & Reheating

Refrigerate 5 days, freeze 3 months. It genuinely improves for the first 48 hours as the spices bloom into the fat.
